title: Add policy-decision authz cache and KMS claim revocation propagator
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce an in-process policy-decision cache + KMS claim revocation propagator to reduce authz latency and improve availability under KMS flapping. Feature gated and rolled out gradually.
commit_summaries: implement LRU TTL cache for policy decisions (cache.go)
add KMS revocation watcher and pubsub invalidation path
unit and integration tests for revocation flows
description:
Motivation: the policy decision path (PD) is a hot path for every API authorization. Frequent checks against the centralized policy engine combined with per-request KMS claim validations caused measurable tail latency and occasional SLO blips when KMS had short interruptions. This PR adds a short-lived in-process policy-decision cache and a revocation propagator that listens for KMS claim revocation events and invalidates cached entries across nodes. The goal is to reduce PD latency and provide graceful degradation when KMS is slow, without weakening security guarantees.

What this change does: 1) pkg/authz/cache.go: LRU+TTL cache keyed by (subject, resource, action, claim-hash); cache stores signed decision blobs with an associated validity window and revocation token. Cache is encrypted in memory using optional mlock-backed buffer when the feature flag is enabled. 2) pkg/kms/revocation_watcher.go: connects to the KMS event stream (pulls from internal KMS CDC topic), normalizes revocation events to a compact revocation ID and publishes invalidation messages to internal pubsub. 3) pkg/net/pubsub_invalidation.go: lightweight subscriber that receives invalidation messages and evicts relevant cache keys. 4) internal/observability/authz_metrics.go: emits cache_hits, cache_misses, cache_evictions, revocation_events_processed, revocation_latency_ms. 5) cmd/agent/flags.go and deploy/feature-flags.yaml: runtime flags and rollout configuration (default off for GA clusters, on in canary). 6) tests: unit coverage for cache eviction and revocation matching; integration scenario that simulates KMS claim revocation and verifies global eviction propagation across two agents using the test harness script scripts/integration/test-revocation.sh. 7) docs/security/authz-cache.md: design doc, rollout plan, and operational runbook.

Compatibility and rollout: gated behind a feature flag (authz.cache.enabled) and two-stage rollout: "canary" -> "regional" -> "global". Cache TTL defaults to 15s for decisions and is configurable per route. The revocation propagator respects backoff and de-dup windows to avoid thundering herd during KMS incident. Designed so that cache failure is transparent: if the cache or propagator fails, we fall back to canonical PD + KMS validation path.

Performance impact: observed median authz latency reduction from 18ms -> 9ms on synthetic workload (PD QPS 3k) and reduced PD QPS to the policy engine by ~58% in canary tests. Metrics dashboards added to Console under Observability -> AuthZ -> cache.

Security considerations: cache stores signed decision blobs and is invalidated immediately on revocation events. The implementation encrypts cache entries in memory by default on hosts with mlock support and clears slices on eviction. We added a security-scan CI step and addressed two medium issues: 1) tight validation of incoming revocation events to avoid blind eviction; 2) hardened parser for claim-hash to avoid injection. Both fixed in this branch.

Review summary / conversation: - Liam O'Connor: requested explicit unit tests for race on concurrent invalidation; addressed in commit "add concurrent invalidation test" and added a data-race test. - Elena Ruiz (security): asked for a threat model doc and confirmation that cached blobs will not be serialized to disk; added docs/security/authz-cache.md and hardened Dockerfile to not enable paging on container images; responded with threat model and mitigations. - Grant Chen (SRE): asked for alerts on revocation lag and an autosilence policy for expected churn during key rotations; added revocation_lag_ms alert and a runbook section describing threshold tuning. - Author responses: implemented backoff, de-dup window, and added a configuration knob authz.cache.max_inflight_evictions to bound memory usage.

CI and stability: initial CI run had a flaky integration test tied to pubsub ordering; workaround added to tests to tolerate eventual ordering semantics and retried integration pool. Final CI: unit/integration/lint/build/security-scan passed.

Merge notes: Feature is merged with squash commit. Rollout plan created in Linear ENG-6221 and post-merge task ENG-6221-2 to enable canary in us-west-2 for 48h before regional ramp. Ops notified via #infra-release and a follow-up runbook review scheduled.

Files changed (high level): added cache and revocation watcher code, pubsub invalidation plumbing, metrics, feature-flag wiring, docs and tests. No public API surface change.
